top_temples.name: Kalyaneshwari Temple, Asansol
top_temples.location_note: Asansol's most famous temple; original structure built in the 3rd century AD by Harigupta.

top_temples.name: Ghaghar Buri Temple
top_temples.location_note: Asansol; the city's oldest temple.

top_temples.name: Maa Muktai Chandi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Asansol city.

top_temples.name: Agni Mandir, Asansol
top_temples.location_note: Asansol; a rare temple dedicated to the god of fire, reflecting the city's industrial character.

top_temples.name: Durga Mandir, Asansol
top_temples.location_note: Asansol city; prominent during Durga Puja.

top_temples.name: Bakreshwar Temple (Vakranath Shiva Temple)
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Paaphra river, Birbhum district; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, built in Oriya-style architecture, famous for eight natural hot springs in the temple courtyard.

top_temples.name: Mahishmardini Temple, Bakreshwar
top_temples.location_note: A distinct shrine within the same Bakreshwar temple complex, housing ancient ASI-preserved paintings of the goddess.

top_temples.name: Mahakal Temple
top_temples.location_note: Darjeeling; blends Hindu and Buddhist worship traditions, one of the town's most visited religious sites.

top_temples.name: Dhirdham Temple
top_temples.location_note: Darjeeling; built 1939 by Rai Saheb Purna Bahadur Pradhan, modeled on the Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu.

top_temples.name: Ghoom Monastery
top_temples.location_note: Near Darjeeling; belongs to the Gelukpa (Yellow Hat) sect, features a 15-ft Maitreya Buddha statue.

top_temples.name: Darjeeling Peace Pagoda
top_temples.location_note: Darjeeling; one of the Japanese-built Peace Pagodas promoting interfaith unity.

top_temples.name: Dali Monastery (Druk Thupten Sangag Choeling)
top_temples.location_note: A few kilometers from Darjeeling town; a newer monastery than Ghoom.

top_temples.name: Kaleshwar Shiva Temple
top_temples.location_note: A remote village in Birbhum district; the tallest Shiva temple in West Bengal, about 500 years old, distinct from the district's Shakti Peetha temples.

top_temples.name: Lord Krishna Temple, Ekachakra
top_temples.location_note: Ekachakra village, about 20 km from Rampurhat in Birbhum district; a historic temple in a scenic setting.

top_temples.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Hooghly River; built 1855 by Rani Rashmoni, closely associated with the saint Ramakrishna Paramahamsa.

top_temples.name: Dwadash Shiva Mandir (Twelve Shiva Temples)
top_temples.location_note: Within the same Dakshineswar temple complex, facing the Ganges opposite the Kuthi Bari.

top_temples.name: Shiv Shakti Dham (Gopalmath Shiv Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Gopalmath neighborhood, Durgapur; the largest temple in the city.

top_temples.name: Bidhan Nagar Ram Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Bidhan Nagar area, Durgapur; set within a large garden.

top_temples.name: Rahreswar Shiv Temple (Arrah Shiv Mandir)
top_temples.location_note: Durgapur; over 800 years old, constructed in 1200 by Maharaja Ballal Sen of the Rarh dynasty, one of the city's oldest landmarks.

top_temples.name: Durgapur ISKCON Temple
top_temples.location_note: 29 Netaji Subhash Road A-Zone, Durgapur.

top_temples.name: Shri Shri Jagannath Temple, Durgapur
top_temples.location_note: One of Durgapur's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Belur Math
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Hooghly in Howrah; headquarters of the Ramakrishna Math and Mission, founded by Swami Vivekananda, blends Hindu, Christian, and Islamic architectural elements.

top_temples.name: Shree Shyam Mandir, Ghusuri
top_temples.location_note: Ghusuridham, Howrah.

top_temples.name: Ramrajatala Ram Temple
top_temples.location_note: Ramrajatala, Howrah.

top_temples.name: Baba Kalyaneshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bally, Howrah district, beside the Grand Trunk Road near the Hooghly river.

top_temples.name: Shri Shri Hajar Haath Kali Mata Temple
top_temples.location_note: Howrah district.

top_temples.name: Jalpesh Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Near Maynaguri, Jalpaiguri district; one of the most visited temples in North Bengal.

top_temples.name: Yogamaya Kali Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jalpaiguri district.

top_temples.name: Rajbari Shib Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jalpaiguri town; formerly owned by the Jalpaiguri Royal family, beside the Rajbari Dighi lake.

top_temples.name: Radha Madhab Temple, Jalpaiguri
top_temples.location_note: Jalpaiguri town; also functions as an ashram.

top_temples.name: Maa Jogomaya and Baba Lokenath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jalpaiguri district, within a busy marketplace.

top_temples.name: Kankalitala Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the banks of the Kopai river near Bolpur/Shantiniketan, Birbhum district; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, marks where Sati's waist is believed to have fallen.

top_temples.name: Ruru Bhairav Shrine
top_temples.location_note: A Shiva lingam shrine near the entrance of the Kankalitala temple complex; the Bhairava associated with this Shakti Peetha.

top_temples.name: Kalighat Kali Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kolkata; one of the 51 Shakti Peethas, present structure dates to the 19th century, one of the city's most sacred sites.

top_temples.name: Birla Mandir, Kolkata
top_temples.location_note: Kolkata; built by the Birla family over 26 years, opened to the public in 1996.

top_temples.name: Parshwanath Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kolkata; established 1867 by Rai Badridas Bahadur Mookim, comprises four distinct structures.

top_temples.name: Thanthania Kalibari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Kolkata; built 1803, especially crowded on Tuesdays and Saturdays.

top_temples.name: Lake Kalibari
top_temples.location_note: Kolkata; established 1949 by Haripada Chakraborty, distinct from Dakshineswar and Belur Math, both of which have their own separate dataset entries.

top_temples.name: Manaskamana Kali Temple
top_temples.location_note: English Bazar town, Malda; an ancient and privileged temple in Malda.

top_temples.name: Maa Jahura Temple (Jauhra Kali)
top_temples.location_note: On the outskirts of Malda town; a historic temple dating to around 1200 AD.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Malda
top_temples.location_note: Mothabari, Malda.

top_temples.name: Madan Mohan Temple, Ramkeli
top_temples.location_note: Ramkeli, Malda district.

top_temples.name: Ramakrishna Math and Mission Ashrama, Malda
top_temples.location_note: Malda town.

top_temples.name: Ramakrishna Temple, Purulia
top_temples.location_note: Vivekanand Nagar area, Purulia; a meditation and spiritual center.

top_temples.name: Deulghata Temples
top_temples.location_note: Purulia district; centuries-old terracotta temple complex.

top_temples.name: Surya Temple, Purulia
top_temples.location_note: On the bank of Saheb Bandh, Purulia; one of the oldest temples in the city.

top_temples.name: Chowk Bazar Soloana Temple
top_temples.location_note: Purulia town.

top_temples.name: Pakbirra Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Purulia district; part of the region's ancient Jain heritage.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Siliguri
top_temples.location_note: Khalpara, Siliguri; one of the largest religious sites in the city.

top_temples.name: Sevokeshwari Kali Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Burdwan Road, Siliguri; open 24 hours.

top_temples.name: Lokenath Mandir, Dagapur
top_temples.location_note: Dagapur, about 5 km from Siliguri; a white-marble shrine popular with devotees from Bangladesh and Bengal.

top_temples.name: Shree Shyam Mandir, Siliguri
top_temples.location_note: Siliguri city.

top_temples.name: Balaji Temple (Hanuman Temple), Khalpara
top_temples.location_note: Khalpara neighborhood, Siliguri; one of the city's oldest temples.

top_temples.name: Maa Tara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Tarapith's central shrine, Birbhum district; a Mahapeeth where Sati's eyeball is believed to have fallen, famed for tantric worship.

top_temples.name: Bamakhepa Ashram/Samadhi
top_temples.location_note: Adjacent to the main Tarapith temple, on the bank of the Dwaraka river; the samadhi and ashram of the revered 'mad saint' who worshipped Tara here.
